# Wormhole stays visible on some waves

## Problem statement

On some (apparently unpatterned) waves the wormhole spawn VFX remains on
screen after every enemy has fully arrived — its close animation never runs
and the graphic stays visible into the next wave. There is no reliable manual
reproduction yet; a root-cause analysis (RCA) is required to identify and fix
the lifecycle bug.

## Users

- **Primary: players** of the shipped game (`PlayScene`). "As a player I expect
  the wormhole that announces each enemy wave to disappear once all enemies
  have arrived, so stale VFX never clutters the arena."
- **Secondary: gym users/developers.** Gym scenes must match the game's spawn
  VFX lifecycle per the gym↔game parity convention (AGENTS.md).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **RCA documented** — the actual root cause is identified (via a
   deterministic regression test that reproduces the stuck wormhole and fails
   before the fix, passes after), and recorded in the work item.
2. **Wormhole always closes** — whenever a wave's enemies have all finished
   growing, the wormhole's close animation runs to completion and the
   container is destroyed and removed from the effects registry — in
   `PlayScene` and every gym formation scene.
3. **At most one live wormhole** — opening a new wormhole (any `spawnWave` /
   formation respawn / transition end) first closes any still-open previous
   wormhole; no path may overwrite `_spawnWormhole` while another is live.
4. **Close survives transitions & respawns** — a wave/level/boss transition,
   wave timeout, wipe→respawn or run reset that begins while the wormhole is
   open still results in a closed, destroyed wormhole (close must not depend
   only on the non-transition update tick).
5. **Gym↔game parity** — the gym formation scenes (including wipe→respawn and
   carry-over paths) enforce the same wormhole lifecycle as the game; a
   regression test covers at least one gym scene alongside `PlayScene`.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes —
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §2.7 (wormhole spawn animation)
   and relevant code comments.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The wormhole timing contract is unchanged: 1 s open + 1.5 s grow + 0.5 s
  close = 3 s spawn-protection window (existing constants in
  `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`).
- No change to spawn positions, wave pacing or gameplay behaviour — this is a
  VFX lifecycle fix only.
- Shared logic must live in the shared core / shared VFX module, consumed by
  both the game and the gyms (parity rule; repo duplicate-body guard).
- Keep the existing deterministic test seams (`finishSpawnAnimations()`,
  `scene.tick(dt)`) working — they are relied on across the scene test
  suites.

## Existing state

- `PlayScene.spawnWave()` opens one wormhole at the first spawn position and
  registers it in `wormholeEffects`; `_updateSpawnAnimations()` closes it once
  `!anySpawning` — but that method is only invoked on non-transition frames
  (`update()` gates it behind `!transitioning`).
- `_onTransitionComplete()` calls `spawnWave()` unconditionally; `spawnWave()`
  has **no guard** to close a previously-open `_spawnWormhole` before
  overwriting it.
- `resetRunState()` sets `_spawnWormhole = null` without destroying the
  container.
- Gyms: `respawnFormation()` / `respawnWithCarriedSurvivors()` rebuild the
  formation without closing an open wormhole (and without re-opening one for
  the fresh entities).

## Desired change

- Close any live wormhole as part of a single, shared lifecycle invariant:
  exactly one live wormhole; it closes (scale→0, alpha→0, destroy, remove
  from registry) once its wave's entities have finished growing — regardless
  of transitions, timeouts, respawns or resets — and any new wormhole first
  cleans up the previous one.
- Add deterministic regression tests covering at least: (a) transition /
  timeout beginning mid-spawn, (b) second `spawnWave()` while one wormhole is
  still live, (c) a gym respawn path.
- Fix in the shared VFX/helper layer where the game and gyms already share
  code; update docs §2.7.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_updateSpawnAnimations()` (close gating),
  `spawnWave()` (open without closing previous), `resetRunState()`/`_loseLife`
  paths.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `respawnFormation()`,
  `respawnWithCarriedSurvivors()`, `_updateSpawnAnimations()`.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — shared open/close lifecycle (candidate home
  for a shared "close if open" guard).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `wormholeEffects` registry init/teardown.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (describe "wormhole spawn animation") and
  `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` (parity describe) — regression
  tests.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §2.7 documentation update.

## Related work

- AH-0MURBER4L00821RR (completed) — the wormhole spawn-animation feature that
  introduced this code; the lifecycle bug is a regression/gap of that feature.
- AH-0MV8BR9Y70079TKC (open) — "Wormhole appears away from player";
  different symptom, same VFX; not blocking, do not absorb.
- AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW (open) — "Enemies should emerge from the wormhole";
  related aesthetics, not blocking, do not absorb.
- AH-0MV9G113S009B37I (in-progress) — "Mystery UFO has no visible
  representation"; picked up by the find-related keyword search but not
  directly related — noted for traceability only.
- AGENTS.md "Gym↔game parity" convention — the parity requirement for this
  fix.
- Automated find-related report (see related-work comment on the work item).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **RCA is the gating risk** — a deterministic repro must be built first;
  without it the fix may address a symptom rather than the leak. Mitigation:
  reproduce the transition/overwrite and respawn paths in tests.
- **Assumption:** the intended lifecycle is exactly one live wormhole per
  wave; over-closing is harmless (close is idempotent after destroy).
- **Risk:** gating the close on the non-transition tick is the core defect —
  the fix must not depend on any single update path.
- **Scope creep:** wormhole positioning (AH-0MV8BR9Y70079TKC) and
  emerge-from-centre (AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW) are tracked separately — out of
  scope here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No interview questions were asked: the seed context ("wormhole stays visible,
  RCA and resolve") combined with code inspection of `PlayScene`,
  `GymFormationScene`, `wormholeSpawn.ts` and the worklog sufficed to draft
  this brief. Any reproduction specifics still unknown (the item notes "I
  cannot discern a pattern") are addressed by the RCA-driven regression test
  (AC1) rather than by further questions.
- OPEN QUESTION: whether the operator can supply a recording/level where the
  stuck wormhole was observed would narrow the RCA; not required to proceed.

## Goal

De-risk the arena's campaign integration (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) before any build work: prove the shared campaign and upgrade-choice systems can run headless under Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses, and identify every impure dependency so the design uses the shared core directly or a named thin adapter — never a divergent copy.

## Headline

A short spike that instantiates/runs the modules the arena will consume — `buildSequencedLevels` (src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts, all fixed/curve/dynamic modes), `sequencer`/`defaultCandidatePool` (src/core/difficultySequencer.ts), `WaveManager` (src/waves/WaveManager.ts), `chooseOptions`/`buildChoiceCandidates` (src/powerups/choice.ts), `MineralHold` (src/core/GameState.ts hold), and the hold-full reward application path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts) — and records exactly which are headless-pure and which need an adapter (e.g. the `EffectsRegistry` the reward applyer requires).

## Context

- The eval layer (src/ai/eval/) must stay pure: no wall clock, no I/O, no Phaser import.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): an enabled behaviour runs the same code in gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Effort-and-risk unknowns recorded on the parent: can `sequencedLevels.ts` run headless without Phaser imports? Can the reward-application path be exercised without a Phaser `EffectsRegistry`?

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A vitest smoke test imports and exercises each target module without importing Phaser or a wall-clock/IO module in the eval entry path; the smoke test lives under src/ai/eval/ (e.g. a `campaignHeadless.test.ts` spike scaffold).
- **AC2:** Every impure dependency found is listed with a concrete adapter plan (thin, named, headless) or a recommendation to not model that behaviour in this item — recorded in a comment on this work item.
- **AC3:** The spike records the design decision the arena build follows: consume each shared entry point directly vs via the named adapter, with the seed derivation (createSeededRng + buildSequencedLevels {seed}) confirmed to be deterministic.
- **AC4:** The spike makes no production code changes outside src/ai/eval/ evaluation-only scaffolding; the finding is reproducible by a maintainer (commands recorded).

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic modes) to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — sequencer + candidate pool to prove headless-safe
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — wave/level state machine to prove headless-safe
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared upgrade-choice flow to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold (capacity/growth/overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (EffectsRegistry dependency to assess)
- `src/ai/eval/campaignHeadless.test.ts` (new vitest spike scaffold) — headless-import smoke coverage

# Phasers spawn in a line then snap to a formation

## Problem statement

When a wave containing orbital Phasers spawns, each Phaser travels from the wave's wormhole to the **grid/line** slot produced by its formation offset (`baseX + col × spacingX`), then **snaps** onto its orbital ring position on the first formation tick. Because a Phaser's orbital phase is derived from `offset.col × (π/2)`, any group larger than four Phasers repeats phases every four members — so with a scaled group (the difficulty sequencer can produce `phaser × 12`) three Phasers stack at each of the four points and the group appears to contain only four entities. The wave is harder to read than intended and the arrival looks broken.

## Users

- **Primary — player:** "As a player I expect a group of Phasers to stream out of the wormhole and settle smoothly onto their final orbital positions, and I expect to see every Phaser in the group, so I can read the telegraphed radial pattern and plan my dodges."
- **Secondary — developer / gym user:** "As a developer I expect the same orbital geometry to drive both the spawn-transit destination and the per-frame orbit, so the gym and the game cannot diverge (gym↔game parity, AGENTS.md)."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **No line then snap** — For an orbital (`phaser`) wave group, every Phaser's wormhole-transit destination is its **live orbital slot**, not the grid/line slot. During the spawn window the Phaser interpolates from the wormhole to its orbital slot and, when the spawn window ends, `applyFormationPosition` places it on that same point with no visible position jump (post-spawn position delta ≤ 1 px).
- **Distinct, evenly distributed phases for any count** — For a group of `N` Phasers, all `N` orbital phases are distinct and evenly distributed across the full turn (`phase_i = i × 2π / N`, `i = 0…N−1`). For `N = 4` this reproduces the existing square (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°); for `N = 12` twelve distinct orbital slots are produced with no two Phasers coincident.
- **Single shared orbital geometry** — One shared pure helper computes the orbital slot and is consumed by both the entity's `applyFormationPosition` and the scene's transit-destination resolver. No duplicated orbital maths (the repo-wide duplicate-body guard passes).
- **Gym↔game parity** — The same behaviour runs in `PlayScene` and in every gym scene that spawns Phasers (`GymFodderEnemies`), verified by tests on both paths.
- **Spawn behaviour otherwise unchanged** — Transit timing is unchanged (completes inside the existing 3 s spawn-protection window), and the existing `isSpawning` gates still apply during transit (bullets pass through, no firing, no body collision, no mineral absorption). The single-live `WormholeController` lifecycle is unchanged.
- **Testing/validation** — New unit tests cover the pure orbital-geometry helper (phase distinctness for `N = 4`, `N = 5`, `N = 12`; slot positions), the Phaser entity's on-ring placement, and the scene-level transit destination (game and gym). A regression test asserts that a >4-member Phaser group produces no coincident slots.
- **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§4.1 E4 Phaser, spawn/formation sections) and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.1 note the count-based orbital phase distribution and the wormhole→orbital-slot transit.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do not change the Phaser's firing pattern, tell/advance-cue behaviour, health, visuals, orbit radius (`PHASER_ORBITAL_RADIUS`), or orbit angular speed (`PHASER_ORBITAL_SPEED`).
- Do not change spawn timing or the 3 s spawn-protection window.
- Do not change other enemies' formation or spawn behaviour; the shared helper must keep a sensible default (4) so single-entity constructors and existing tests are unaffected.
- Gym↔game parity: shared behaviour lives once in the shared core/helpers and is consumed by both the game and the gyms (AGENTS.md).
- Keep the pure orbital-geometry helper free of Phaser runtime dependencies so it is unit-testable.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Phaser.ts`
  - `_computeOrbitalPhase(offset)` returns `(offset.row × 10 + offset.col) × PHASER_ORBITAL_PHASE_SPACING`, with `PHASER_ORBITAL_PHASE_SPACING = π/2` — only four distinct phases, so counts > 4 collide.
  - `applyFormationPosition(baseX, baseY, dt, _spacingX, _spacingY)` treats the formation base as the orbit centre and places the body at `(centre + PHASER_ORBITAL_RADIUS·cos θ, centre + PHASER_ORBITAL_RADIUS·sin θ)` with `θ = phase + _localPhase × PHASER_ORBITAL_SPEED`. Spacing is intentionally ignored.
- `src/utils/formations.ts` — `buildOrbitalPhaseOffsets(count)` returns `{ row: 0, col: i }` for `i = 0…count−1` (a line when fed through `computeFormationPosition`). There is no shared orbital-slot helper.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_spawnEnemy(spawn, origin)` starts the wormhole transit with a destination resolver that computes `baseX + offset.col × spacingX`, `baseY + offset.row × spacingY`. For orbital offsets this is a horizontal line, hence the snap when `applyFormationPosition` takes over.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_spawnFormation(offsets)` uses the same grid destination resolver (`formationBaseX + offset.col × spacingX`, …), with the same snap.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — `SpawnState`/`updateSpawnAnimation` already support a live per-frame destination (`destFn`), so the fix can resolve the orbital slot every frame without new transit machinery.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — `planGroupSpawns` derives offsets from `groupDef.count` but `EnemySpawn` does **not** carry the group count, so the per-entity config never learns how many Phasers are in its group.
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — the Phaser candidate scales `count` from `max(1, floor(4 × 0.1))` up to `min(200, ceil(4 × 3)) = 12`; `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts` records generated waves such as `phaserx12`, confirming >4-member groups occur in the shipped campaign.

## Desired change

- Add a **shared, pure** orbital-geometry helper (in `src/utils/formations.ts` alongside `computeFormationPosition`) that, given an orbital offset/phase index and the group count, returns the phase fraction/angle, and given the base + count + radius + elapsed angle returns the world slot. Both the entity and the transit-destination resolver must call it (Q3 = generic fix).
- Thread the group count to the orbital geometry so `N` is known at construction and at spawn planning. Candidates: an optional count/phase field on `FormationOffset` (populated by `buildOrbitalPhaseOffsets`), or an optional `formationCount` on `EnemySpawn` → `createEnemyFromConfig` → `PhaserConfig`. Default to 4 when absent.
- Change `PhaserEntity._computeOrbitalPhase` to distribute phases evenly using the group count, and expose an optional **formation-slot seam** (e.g. `formationSlot(baseX, baseY)`) that returns the entity's live orbital point.
- In `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` and `GymFormationScene._spawnFormation`, for entities exposing the orbital slot seam, resolve the transit destination to the **live orbital slot** (re-evaluated each frame via the existing `destFn`) instead of the grid line; leave every other enemy's destination unchanged.
- Update the docs and add the tests listed in the Acceptance Criteria.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/formations.ts` — New shared pure orbital-slot/phase helper; possibly extend `buildOrbitalPhaseOffsets` to carry the group count while preserving its offset ordering.
- `src/entities/Phaser.ts` — Count-based phase distribution; `applyFormationPosition` uses the shared helper; expose the optional formation-slot seam.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — `EnemySpawn` (optionally) carries the group count from `planGroupSpawns`.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` — Thread the group count into `PhaserConfig` (if that route is chosen).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_spawnEnemy` orbital transit destination.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_spawnFormation` orbital transit destination.
- `src/entities/Phaser.test.ts` — on-ring placement + distinct phase coverage.
- `src/utils/formations.test.ts` — pure orbital-geometry helper tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.test.ts` — scene-level transit-destination and parity tests.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §4.1 E4 Phaser and the spawn/formation sections.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.1 E4 Phaser orbital behaviour.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** (open) — *Enemies should emerge from the wormhole*. Generic wormhole→formation transit; parent epic. **Partial overlap only**: it defines the transit mechanism generically, whereas this item fixes the orbital destination and the phase distribution for Phasers.
- **AH-0MVDW3T9R0054HG6** (open) — *Implement wormhole transit movement, parity and docs*, the epic's implementation child.
- **AH-0MVDW2N6Y009DUY5** (completed) — *Unit tests for wormhole-to-formation transit movement*.
- **AH-0MURBER4L00821RR** (completed) — wormhole VFX, 1 px growth and spawn-protection gates.
- **AH-0MV8BR9Y70079TKC** (completed) — wave-portal placement and formation anchoring.
- **AH-0MVDW3R7300979DC** (completed) — drop placement avoids the formation slots of mid-emergence enemies.
- **AH-0MV2SGIX5005PFJT** (completed) — per-level archetype repetition cap (why a Phaser group can still scale to twelve).
- AGENTS.md **Gym↔game parity** convention and the `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption (Q1 = A):** A single ring with phases evenly distributed using the group's actual count. For `N = 4` this preserves the existing square; larger groups spread around the same 80 px ring.
- **Assumption (Q2 = A):** Phasers transit directly from the wormhole to their orbital slot (no line phase).
- **Assumption (Q3 = A):** The fix is generic in the shared orbital-formation path, with Phaser as the only current consumer.
- **Risk:** `applyFormationPosition` advances `_localPhase` during the spawn window, so the live orbital point moves while the Phaser transits. The destination must be resolved per frame (the existing `destFn` supports this) or a position pop will appear at the end of the window.
- **Risk:** Threading the group count to the E4 geometry touches the spawn-planning pipeline. Mitigation: default to 4 and make the new field optional so single-entity constructors and existing callers/tests are unchanged.
- **Risk:** Adding an optional field to `FormationOffset` can break strict `toEqual` assertions in `formations.test.ts`; update those tests deliberately (and prefer a route that keeps `FormationOffset` minimal if a lower-impact option exists).
- **Scope creep:** Do not add multi-ring orbits, particle trails, new VFX, or change the Phaser's firing/telegraph behaviour; record any such idea as a separate linked work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — How should phasers be arranged when the group has more than four members?** (options: A evenly distribute phases across the single ring using the group's actual count; B multiple concentric rings; C cap the group count at 4) — **Answer (producer):** A. Source: interactive reply, this intake session.
- **Q2 — What should the spawn behaviour be?** (options: A emerge from the wormhole and travel directly to the orbital slot, no line/snap; B keep the line spawn and ease into the orbit after the spawn window) — **Answer (producer):** A. Source: interactive reply, this intake session.
- **Q3 — Scope of the orbital-phase fix?** (options: A generic shared orbital-formation helper; B Phaser only) — **Answer (producer):** A. Source: interactive reply, this intake session.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched `wl search "phaser formation"`, `"spawn formation"`, `"orbital phase"`, `"phasers overlap"` and reviewed the candidates. Closest was **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** (*Enemies should emerge from the wormhole*): its ACs cover the generic wormhole→formation transit and do not address (a) the orbital destination for Phasers or (b) the phase-per-count collision. **No full duplicate found**; this item is scoped to the phaser-specific orbital defect and cross-referenced to the transit epic.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVDW3T9R0054HG6** – Implement wormhole transit movement, parity and docs (open)
- **AH-0MUJKJ8OO007TBSS** – Single-formation wave groups can declare more enemies than they spawn (completed)
- **AH-0MUGCQ8MS000815U** – Remove fixed asteroid group from Formations.ts (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv2sgix5005pfjt, absent, absorption, acceptance, actual (+357 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mv2sgix5005pfjt, absent, absorption, actual, add (+348 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mugzdtfx004rbd1, 0murber4l00821rr, 0mv2sgix5005pfjt, 0mv8br9y70079tkc, absent (+345 more)

## Goal

As a player, when I change the control scheme in Settings and then continue playing, the chosen scheme must be used by the ship — not only from the next run. Today, a scheme change made from the in-game Settings (pause menu) is persisted but the live ship keeps the old scheme for the rest of the run, so the chosen scheme is 'present but not honoured in gameplay'.

## Investigation (evidence)

Reproduced in a real headless Chromium against the current dev source (build -> boot -> play):

- Saving ai_hell_settings.controlScheme = 'fourDirectional' before starting a game -> PlayScene spawns the ship with fourDirectional (holding A translates, no rotation). **Works.**
- Saving 'asteroids' -> spawns asteroids (holding A rotates, no translation). **Works.**
- Full UI flow: Menu -> Settings -> cycle Control Scheme row -> Back -> Play -> the ship uses the new scheme. **Works.**
- Pause-menu flow: Play -> Esc -> Settings -> change scheme -> quit to menu -> Play -> ship uses the new scheme. **Works.**
- **Pause-menu mid-run flow: Play -> Esc -> Settings -> change scheme -> Back -> Resume -> the live ship keeps the OLD scheme for the rest of the run** (verified: scheme at start 'asteroids', stored becomes 'fourDirectional', live scheme after resume is still 'asteroids'). **Defect.**

Root cause: PlayScene resolves and applies the scheme once at ship spawn in create() (commit d45df97c, AC4 of AH-0MVI7LRCJ006Q8SA). On RESUME (returning from the pause menu) only _applyBindings() re-applies key bindings; the control scheme is deliberately not re-applied mid-run (intake decision Q2(a): 'applies on the next run / next ship spawn, never mid-run'). The operator's expectation ('When playing a game the chosen control scheme should be used') requires the chosen scheme to be honoured while the game is being played.

## Proposed implementation

- On PlayScene RESUME (or when the pause menu closes back into the run), resolve the effective scheme with resolvePlayerControlScheme(loadStoredControlScheme(), loadShipConfig()) and apply it to the live ship when it differs (Player.setScheme already swaps the movement model and input shape live; input dispatch reads player.getScheme() via the shared mapControlInput seam, so gym game parity is preserved).
- Keep spawn-time application as-is; a changed scheme therefore takes effect immediately on returning to the running game AND on the next run.
- Update the AC4 scene test that currently asserts 'does not swap the current ship when the setting changes mid-run' to the new expected behaviour; update docs (GDD §2.2, README) and the parent work item's AC4 note.
- Note: this reverses the recorded intake decision Q2(a) ('never mid-run') — needs operator confirmation before implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Changing the Control Scheme in the in-game Settings and resuming applies the chosen scheme to the live ship immediately (movement model + input mapping switch; verified by a scene test: saved fourDirectional then set mid-run -> the live ship drives four-directionally without a new run).
- AC2: Spawn-time behaviour is unchanged: a setting saved before a run still drives the ship from the first frame; resolution precedence (player setting -> ship config -> built-in default) unchanged.
- AC3: Bindings (rebindable keys) are unaffected; the shared mapControlInput seam is the only scheme->input mapping (gym game parity guards still pass).
- AC4: Settings row/save/restore behaviour unchanged; no CSV/config mutation.
- AC5: Full project test suite passes.

## Key files (predicted)

- src/scenes/PlayScene.ts — apply the resolved scheme on RESUME (and any other in-run settings-return path).
- src/scenes/PlayScene.controlScheme.test.ts — replace the mid-run no-change assertion with the new mid-run application assertion (additive: cover both 'applies on resume' and 'also applies on next run').
- docs/Game Design Document.md, README.md — note that a scheme change applies to the running game on resume (replaces 'next run only').
- Parent AH-0MVI7LRCJ006Q8SA AC4 wording/decision note to be updated (additive clarification).

data.description:
## Goal

As a player/operator, changing the Control Scheme in Settings must actually persist. Today it silently fails once the browser's localStorage quota is full, because the dev telemetry sink fills that quota. The fix removes telemetry from localStorage entirely: the dev JSONL sink becomes an **in-memory, per-run buffer** that is uploaded straight from memory and reset at the start of each run.

## Operator report (verbatim)

> AH-0MVIMPC11001F7WU is still not working. It seems the setting is not being saved. 1) selecting settings and change to 4 directional 2) back to menu 3) open settings and the control profile is back to asteroids

Environment (operator-confirmed): `npm run dev -- --host`, playing at http://100.106.5.111:5173/. The row visibly shows Four Directional after the change, then reverts to Asteroids after re-opening Settings.

Related: discovered-from:AH-0MVIMPC11001F7WU (mid-run scheme honouring, commit 3c75eb4c) and AH-0MVI7LRCJ006Q8SA (the control-scheme setting feature).

## Root cause (confirmed from the operator's console)

```
Uncaught QuotaExceededError: Failed to execute 'setItem' on 'Storage':
Setting the value of 'ai_hell_settings' exceeded the quota.
    at saveSettings (settingsStore.ts:262)
    at SettingsScene._persist (SettingsScene.ts:745)
    at SettingsScene.setControlScheme ...
```

Measured on current `dev` (headless Chromium, normal play): ~50.8 telemetry ticks/s at ~1,267 B/tick = **~64 KB/s** written to `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`. The ~5 MiB per-origin quota is exhausted after **~1.4 minutes of play**. From that moment every `localStorage.setItem` throws — including `saveSettings` — so the Control Scheme (and any other setting) silently fails to persist and reverts to the last saved value.

Three defects share this cause:

1. **Settings become unsaveable** once the quota fills (the reported symptom).
2. **Silent telemetry truncation**: `recorder.deliver` counts sink-write failures (`failedBatches`) without throwing, so a long run is quietly head-truncated; any single run longer than ~65 s cannot fit in localStorage at all.
3. **Cross-run duplication in uploaded recordings**: nothing clears the sink between runs, and the run-end upload POSTs the **whole accumulated sink**. Run 2's `recordings/session-*.jsonl` therefore contains runs 1+2, run 3's all three — the recordings double-count and the automatic evaluation sees stale records.

## Approach (operator-approved rescope — supersedes the earlier "cap the sink" plan)

Telemetry must not use localStorage at all. Design:

1. **Dev JSONL sink becomes in-memory and per-run.** `createTelemetrySink`'s `jsonl` case creates a run-scoped in-memory writer (the existing `createMemoryLineWriter()` in `src/telemetry/sinks.ts` already provides the primitive) instead of `createLocalStorageLineWriter(...)`. The buffer is **reset on `startRun`**, so each run starts clean — this is the operator's "clear it at the start of the next game" and it removes both the cross-run duplication and any need for a cap/eviction policy.
2. **Upload from memory.** `uploadDevTelemetry` reads the in-memory buffer content via an injected `readSink` seam (already the shape of `DevTelemetryUploadOptions.readSink`) wired to the recorder's buffer, instead of `localStorage.getItem(...)`. Endpoint, content type, NDJSON body and the run-end fire-and-forget behaviour are unchanged, so `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` and the evaluation pipeline need no change.
3. **Expose the buffer to the dev CLI tooling.** The three Node scripts currently read the run via `page.evaluate(localStorage.getItem('ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl'))`. Add a dev-gated page accessor following the existing `window.__aiHellScenario` / `window.__aiHellRunState` convention — e.g. `window.__aiHellTelemetry = { read(): string }` installed by the dev-gated wiring, never written in a production bundle (same static-elimination pattern as `loadDevTelemetryUploader`). Update:
   - `scripts/record-session.mjs` (read the run out of the page),
   - `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (pre-clip reset + post-clip read; the pre-boot `removeItem` becomes a buffer reset/no-op),
   - `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` (assert against the page buffer instead of the localStorage key).
   `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` is file/stdin based — unaffected.
4. **Harden `saveSettings` as a cheap safety net.** Wrap the `setItem` in `src/core/settingsStore.ts` so a full or unavailable storage can never throw out of a Phaser input handler; on failure log one clear `console.warn`. This is defence in depth: with telemetry off localStorage, the settings record is the only writer left.
5. **Update the pinned contract + docs.** `src/telemetry/devUpload.test.ts` pins "sink content left intact after a successful upload"; replace that with the stronger "the dev sink never touches localStorage" (plus "a run start resets the buffer"). Update `docs/TELEMETRY.md` and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, which document the localStorage key.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/telemetry/sinks.ts` — memory sink as the `jsonl` default; keep/rescope `createLocalStorageLineWriter` (it becomes unused by the runtime path; per the coding disciplines, report rather than silently delete — decide explicitly whether to keep it as exported test-covered API or remove it).
- `src/telemetry/recorder.ts` / `src/telemetry/index.ts` — buffer access + reset-on-`startRun` seam.
- `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts` — read from memory (default `readSink`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (or the `runTelemetry` wire-up) — install the dev-gated `window.__aiHellTelemetry` accessor.
- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` — quota-defensive `saveSettings`.
- `scripts/record-session.mjs`, `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`, `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs`.
- Tests: `src/telemetry/sinks.test.ts`, `devUpload.test.ts`, `recorder.test.ts`, `settingsStore` tests, plus the script tests.
- Docs: `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The dev telemetry path never reads or writes localStorage — no `setItem`/`getItem` on `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl` from the runtime path (unit test asserts the resolved `jsonl` sink is the in-memory writer and that recording + upload complete with `localStorage` unavailable).
- AC2: Each run's uploaded body contains **only that run's** records: `startRun` resets the buffer (unit test: two sequential runs, second upload has exactly one `run_header` and no records from the first run).
- AC3: With localStorage pre-filled to overflow, changing the Control Scheme in Settings persists and reopening Settings shows the new value, with no `QuotaExceededError` in the console (browser-level check, menu and pause origins).
- AC4: A single run of arbitrary length is captured in full (no quota-based truncation); the buffer is released on run end after upload.
- AC5: `npm run record`, `npm run capture` (action-intensity series export) and `npm run verify-dev-telemetry` still work end-to-end against the new page accessor; `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` behaviour unchanged.
- AC6: `saveSettings` never throws out of an input handler; a residual storage failure logs exactly one clear `console.warn`.
- AC7: Docs (`docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`) describe the in-memory per-run buffer and no longer claim a localStorage key; the dev gating of the page accessor is documented and enforced (no accessor in a production bundle).
- AC8: Full project test suite passes (`/skill:test --type full` at the dev-push gate).

## Out of scope / follow-up

- **Incremental (per-batch) upload for crash resilience**: with in-memory buffering, a page reload/crash mid-run loses the un-uploaded tail (today it survives a reload but silently stops at the quota). Streaming batches to the dev server would recover at most one batch (~1.3 s) of loss; raised as a separate discovered-from item rather than folded in here.
- **Cutting the production/player tick rate to ~4 Hz (0.25 s)**: separate decision (prefer a time-based `TICK_INTERVAL_MS` over the current per-tick probability `VITE_TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_RATE`); not required by this fix, since production telemetry is consent-gated and uses the remote sink (no localStorage).
